trap-superlative.notes: STANDING-TRAP FINDING, structural, do not fix inline. Recomputed at mpmath dps=30, proton pin q_0 = 1.1099785827513808, h = 0.2090602988. (1) Bare: net = 1 + h = 1.209060299, matching the quoted 1.209. The quoted shortfall (1.022 - 1.006)/1.022 = 1.566% is right for the quoted MeV values. (2) BUT the net-to-MeV conversion is NEVER STATED. Going from net 1.209 to 1.006 MeV implies 0.83205114 MeV per net unit, a constant that appears nowhere in the block, has no citation and no witness field - so the entire '1.6% short' claim rests on an unstated conversion. (3) With that implied constant, matching 2m_e needs net = 1.228289886, hence phi = 0.0538675 and s = 0.108282. The block quotes phi = 0.0487 and s = 0.0978, both low by a factor 1.106-1.107. (4) Worse, the quoted values give net_linear = 1.205278412 and net_circular = 1.205164840, both BELOW the bare 1.209060299. Under any increasing net-to-energy map the coloured configurations therefore have LESS energy than the bare pair and cannot close a shortfall - they widen it (E = 1.0029 and 1.0028 MeV against the bare 1.006). (5) Separately, phi and s are FITTED to 2m_e by construction ('Setting E_pair = 2m_e fixes phi = 0.0487'), so 'both models close the gap' would be a tautology even with correct values, not a prediction. (6) The algebra itself is CORRECT and was verified term by term: the five normal-form coefficients, net = (1 + phi_0 + phi_1)(1 + psi_0 + psi_1) + (phi_0 psi_0 + phi_1 psi_1)h, and both polarization specialisations all check out.
